transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Diego Chen (Redwood SE), Rebecca Lin (Northstar), Marcus Holt (Northstar), Priya Kapoor (Northstar)

Summary: quick weekly sync on the POC quality eval; reviewed latest prompt sets and scoring, looked at regressions vs baseline, discussed guardrails and PHI concerns, outlined next steps to tighten prompts and run larger regression sweep.

Topics: prompt sets, automatic scoring thresholds, hallucination cases, guardrails (blocklist vs classifier), PHI handling, rollout plan for dedicated pool benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Rebecca, Marcus, Priya — good to see you. Diego and I are here from Redwood to run through the quality eval results from the last batch. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Rebecca Lin: Good, thanks. Busy week but we're ready to go.
[00:18] Marcus Holt: Morning. real quick, we had one noisy dataset issue but should be fine now.
[00:25] Diego Chen: Perfect, great. I'll share my screen — the scoring spreadsheet and the latest run we did on the 1k test set. Note: there are a couple of rows where the auto-score flagged a false positive on the guardrail.
[00:38] Ava Martinez: Quick reminder — last week we tuned the prompt templates to reduce instruction leakage and added the top-2 guardrail classifier. This run folds those changes in.
[00:49] Marcus Holt: I noticed in the summary emails that overall F1 went up but precision on clinical terms dropped a bit?
[00:55] Diego Chen: Yeah that's right. F1 improves because recall increased, but precision dipped on clinical-entity extraction. We suspect it's from the more permissive assistant instruction in prompt variant C.
[01:10] Rebecca Lin: Can you show an example?
[01:13] Diego Chen: Sure, here's a sample. Prompt: "Summarize patient encounter, keep PHI redacted." Model output: "Patient is a 46-year-old male with pancreatitis, prescribed amoxicillin." The guardrail classifier flagged 'pancreatitis' as clinical and expected redaction, but the prompt returned a raw mention.
[01:30] Priya Kapoor: That's a compliance issue for us. We need PHI redaction to be deterministic — can't rely on soft prompts alone.
[01:38] Ava Martinez: Understood. Two things we discussed before: 1) explicit redaction post-processing (regex + entity model) and 2) stronger guardrail classifier threshold. We can combine both.
[01:48] Marcus Holt: Post-processing helps but sometimes the entity model misses context so we still see leakage. How feasible is adding a hard-blocklist on certain terms?
[01:57] Diego Chen: We can do a hybrid approach: first pass through the classifier, if confidence below X then apply entity-based redaction, and separately run a blocklist for critical PHI keywords. Blocklist risks false positives though, like 'diabetes' in general analytics.
[02:12] Rebecca Lin: Right, we don't want to over-redact and lose clinical utility. Tuning threshold is critical. What's the tradeoff numbers?
[02:18] Diego Chen: In the run we showed, at classifier threshold 0.85 we saw PHI leakage rate of ~0.6% but recall for clinical summarization dropped 4 points. At 0.75 leakage rose to 1.9% but recall recovered.
[02:33] Ava Martinez: So decision: we can set classifier to 0.85 for the pilot to prioritize compliance, then re-evaluate. Diego, can you run a larger regression at that threshold?
[02:41] Diego Chen: Yep, I'll run a 5k sample sweep with classifier at 0.85 and the post-processing pipeline enabled. Expect results by Monday.
[02:49] Marcus Holt: Good. Another area: hallucinations in medication suggestions. We saw a handful of outputs where the model invented dosing.
[02:58] Priya Kapoor: Invented dosing is high risk. We need guardrails that block any numeric medication suggestion unless it's present in source notes.
[03:07] Diego Chen: We can add instruction-level constraints and a check that the output only echoes medications from the input. If tokens not in input are present, the post-processing flags and either redacts or inserts a caution.
[03:20] Rebecca Lin: Could we have the assistant default to "no dosing provided in notes" style responses when unsure?
[03:25] Ava Martinez: Yes, we recommended that in the runbook — an explicit safe-fail token and a canned fallback. We'll add the fallback template to the prompt set.
[03:33] Marcus Holt: About scoring, what's the human-in-the-loop plan? We want to prioritize edge cases for manual review, not dump everything.
[03:41] Diego Chen: The scoring spreadsheet marks high-impact failures: PHI leakage, hallucinated dosing, and incorrect diagnosis mapping. We can add a severity score column and sample for manual review by severity bucket.
[03:52] Rebecca Lin: That works. Also, for traceability we need per-request audit fields: model version, prompt id, classifier score. Are those included?
[03:59] Ava Martinez: Yes, Redwood runtime already logs model variant, prompt template id, classifier score, and guardrail decision. We can map those to your audit schema. I'll attach the mapping doc.
[04:10] Priya Kapoor: On the security side, we still need to confirm data residency and KMS integration for key material if we go to Dedicated/Private. Any updates?
[04:19] Diego Chen: For Dedicated we can provision a VPC with customer-controlled KMS; for Private on-prem we support HSM integration but that will push timeline. For the POC we're ok with short-lived logs retained in our region, but we'll provide a SOC2 report and data flow diagram.
[04:33] Rebecca Lin: Please send the SOC2 and the data flow diagram — that's a blocker for procurement.
[04:38] Ava Martinez: We'll send both today.
[04:41] Marcus Holt: Latency question: when we move to a dedicated pool, what does tail latency look like at our typical batch size?
[04:47] Diego Chen: On the Dedicated baseline we saw 95th percentile of ~220ms for single-turn summarization with continuous batching enabled; with KV cache and quantization it can get lower. But real-world numbers depend on sequence length and batch mix. We can run a light-load benchmark on your 1k sample.
[05:03] Rebecca Lin: Please do — schedule for mid-August. Also want cost estimate for running at 500k tokens/day.
[05:09] Ava Martinez: We'll provide a cost projection in the pricing workbook.
[05:12] Priya Kapoor: One more compliance point: retention and audit retention window. We need logs for 7 years for some trials. Can Redwood accommodate long-term retention?
[05:21] Diego Chen: Long-term retention is possible as an add-on; default retention is 90 days but enterprise add-ons support long-term S3 archive with encryption. We'll include retention options in the doc.
[05:33] Rebecca Lin: Great. For the regression results you mentioned earlier, what does the delta look like vs the baseline model?
[05:39] Diego Chen: Compared to the baseline (model v1.2 without guardrails), the new prompt + classifier reduced hallucination rate by ~34% and improved overall ROUGE-L by 2.1 points, but clinical-entity precision dropped by 3.8 points in one variant.
[05:54] Marcus Holt: Sounds like net positive but need to address the precision.
[05:58] Ava Martinez: Agreed. Action items are to tighten classifier threshold, add post-processing, and run the larger regression. We'll also add the fallback template.
[06:08] Priya Kapoor: Also need to test edge cases where notes contain abbreviations and nested PHI — those tend to trip the entity model.
[06:15] Marcus Holt: I'll upload 1k edge-case prompts by Friday.
[06:19] Rebecca Lin: Ok last thing — can we get a short tech note on how Redwood's guardrail classifier is trained and whether it uses customer data in training? This is a procurement question.
[06:29] Diego Chen: Short answer: the guardrail classifier in the POC is a Redwood-managed model trained on synthetic and public datasets; it does not incorporate customer PII in training. We'll provide a short write-up and the model card.
[06:40] Ava Martinez: Alright, thanks everyone. Quick recap of next steps in chat and we'll follow up with the spreadsheets and SOC2.
[06:47] Rebecca Lin: Thanks all.
[06:49] End of meeting.
